title: Fix it: collapse a list of lists into one list
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You are given an array of arrays. Each inner array contains items.

Return a single flat array with all the items merged together, but STOP after one level of nesting.

If an item is itself an array (nested deeper), it stays as-is — do not flatten recursively.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
uses map which keeps the structure

explanation.approach: `flatten` collapses exactly one level of nesting — no more, no less. If you have a doubly-nested structure, one level stays. This is by design: it lets you flatten a list of lists without recursing into the items.

snippets.label: A list of lists with simple items
snippets.note: Three arrays nested inside one. The job is to merge them.

snippets.label: The answer — flatten
snippets.note: `flatten` opens up exactly one level, spilling all the items into a single array.

snippets.label: When an item is itself nested deeper
snippets.note: The doubly-nested `[2, 3]` stays as-is. `flatten` does exactly one level — see the trap in the curriculum.

snippets.label: If you want to flatten and transform together
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload flatMap ((arr) -> arr map ($ * 2))
snippets.note: `flatMap` applies a function to each element and then flattens one level. Here we transform each inner array by doubling its numbers, then flatten. The end result is: apply map to each inner array, then merge the results.

snippets.label: Empty arrays inside
snippets.note: Empty arrays contribute nothing to the flattened result — they just disappear.
